reputation.summary: A niche hobbyist part. ADI pitched the AD744 for demanding audio (0.0003% THD, 13 MHz) and as a fast-settling buffer for 12/14-bit DACs and ADCs. Tangent's CMoy survey (via Soomal) lists it at $4.52, needing 6.8 V for 0.5 V into 33 Ω, with no listening verdict. It is best known as the donor die in fake OPA627s.
typical_uses: Fast-settling buffers for 12/14-bit DACs and ADCs
DAC I/V and line stages (reportedly; no community source)
caveats: AD744 compensation pin has no OPA627 counterpart: not a clean OPA627 substitute. Check pin function before rolling.
Noise about 3× the OPA627's (ZeptoBars); ADI's LTspice model uses ~16 nV/√Hz.
Offset higher than the OPA627: 0.5 mV vs 0.1 mV (ZeptoBars).
Weak headphone driver in Tangent's table: 6.8 V needed for 0.5 V into 33 Ω.

counterfeit_notes: Genuine AD744 dies get remarked as OPA627: ZeptoBars (April 2014) found one, with a single laser-trimmed resistor, in a ~$2 eBay 'OPA627'. Spot them by ~3× noise, 0.5 mV offset, 3.5 mA supply current (OPA627 ~7 mA) or decap.
